plan.title: Paired within-subject DE: treated vs control blood
plan.analytical_narrative: Design: 5 subjects, each contributing a control and a treated blood sample (paired, n=10 samples, 12000 genes, raw STAR/featureCounts integer counts). The research question ('which genes respond to treatment within each subject') is answered by a within-subject paired comparison, which removes between-subject variability from the test. Track 1 loads and QCs the count matrix and metadata, verifies pairing and sample identity, and runs a blind-VST PCA/sample-distance check to confirm samples cluster by subject and separate by condition before any modeling. Track 2 fits DESeq2 with design ~subject + condition (subject as a blocking term, condition as the term of interest, control as the explicit reference level), runs the Wald test on the condition coefficient, applies apeglm shrinkage to the reported log2 fold changes, and selects genes by BH-adjusted p-value < 0.05 with independent filtering left on. Track 3 takes the full ranked gene list (Wald statistic) into fgsea preranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark (2026.1) and Reactome (current) gene sets for human, reporting leading-edge genes and collapsing redundant sets. Track 4 assembles the final report with both fit diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot), the p-value histogram, the reproducibility record (sessionInfo, seed, package/collection versions), and the full DE + enrichment tables. All choices (design formula, reference level, filtering threshold, ranking statistic for GSEA) are grounded in the returned procedure from the knowledge service for a paired 5-vs-5 human bulk RNA-seq design with STAR/featureCounts counts.

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind=TRUE), PCA, sample distance heatmap

design = ~subject + condition, explicit reference level control
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, Hallmark then Reactome
Combined DE + enrichment report with diagnostics and reproducibility record
